A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same MAC-Tuning research work, with 14 complete, readable pages including Appendices A.1–A.10. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable assessment of all dimensions.

before.justification: v2.pdf reports original MAC-Tuning experiments across six datasets, baseline comparisons, human evaluation in Section 3.10, and additional empirical analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v3.pdf retains the original benchmark results, human evaluation, case studies, and appendix experiments, including the large-question-count results in Table 8.

M1.justification: Section 2 retains identical multi-problem data construction, confidence labeling, and sequential fine-tuning for answer prediction and confidence estimation. No method component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CoQA, ParaRel, GSM, MMLU, MTI-Bench, and SQA under the same independent, sequential, transfer, and varying-question-count scenarios.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets are identical: LLaMA3, QA-Only, Single-QA, and Merge-AC in Table 1, and the same vanilla-model comparisons in Tables 5–8. Single-QA remains excluded from sequential datasets.

E3.justification: Dataset splits and counts, AP/ECE/accuracy definitions, model configurations, training settings, question-count protocols, and the 100-example human evaluation are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices.

E4.justification: Both versions contain identical component ablations, out-of-domain evaluations, question-count and transfer analyses, model comparisons, and case studies. Appendix A.9 retains the same large-question-count analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain point-estimate reporting without repeated-run counts, seed information, error bars, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. No statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match. For example, Table 1 retains MAC-Tuning’s CoQA AP/ECE of 69.8/7.33, and Section 3.10 retains human-verified accuracy of 89.2% for certain answers and 41.2% for uncertain answers. Appendix results also match.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and training objectives in Section 2, including Equations (1)–(2), and the AP/ECE formulas in Appendix A.5 are identical. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs change.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion are unchanged, including the claimed novelty of multi-problem confidence estimation and the reported AP advantage of up to 25%.

C2.justification: Interpretations of separate answer/confidence learning, task difficulty, transfer, and scalability remain identical. The limitations concerning prompt sensitivity, resource-constrained coverage, alternative explanations, and possible undertraining at large question counts are retained.

D1.justification: Appendices A.3–A.6 retain the same templates, data details, calculation instructions, LoRA settings, and A100-40GB hardware disclosure. The first-page code/resource link is unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference entries, and related-work discussion in Appendix A.2 are identical. Positioning relative to confidence calibration and previous multi-problem approaches does not change.

P1.justification: On page 1, Qingyun Wang’s affiliation changes from University of Illinois to William & Mary, and the Illinois affiliation is expanded to University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. The arXiv version/date stamp also changes. All substantive prose and section structure remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–8 retain identical content, formatting, captions, and placement. Page and column organization are unchanged; the first-page edits only replace affiliation and version text.

improvement.justification: v3.pdf updates institutional affiliations and the version stamp while retaining identical methods, evidence, explanations, limitations, and appendices. These administrative edits do not materially change the paper’s overall scientific quality or readability.
